page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-32 is a flexible compute instance featuring the arm64 architecture. Powered by the Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor, this shape provides 4 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core. It is configured with 32.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The instance includes no local storage and does not feature hardware GPU acceleration, but provides one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show balanced general compute capabilities with distinct profile characteristics. The Ampere Altra cores achieve middle-tier ratings on stress-ng single-core (1781.38) and multi-core (7033.9) tests, alongside average throughput in large block uncached memory read (48.11 GB/sec) and write (28.35 GB/sec) benchmarks. However, Geekbench metrics (1118.0 single-core, 3734.0 multi-core) and PassMark CPU metrics (3164.84 overall) place within lower percentiles, reflecting the lower instructions-per-clock profile of the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture when evaluated against high-power x86 alternatives. Static web serving throughput reaches 6.7 GB/sec, placing it in the middle tier.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides significant memory capacity relative to compute density, offering qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require higher RAM allocation without demanding high single-thread compute. The dedicated core topology ensures deterministic CPU execution without hyper-threading contention.

VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-32 is well aligned with memory-heavy mid-scale workloads, including in-memory caching tiers, database servers, web serving, microservices, and general-purpose ARM-native software build environments.

Its high memory capacity per core provides strong qualitative resource density for memory-oriented application hosting, in-memory databases, and containerized microservices.
